cohort: The study included 161 intrapartum maternal deaths in Japan between 2010 and 2022, comparing those who received labor analgesia (cases) with those who did not (controls).
finding: Among maternal deaths, amniotic fluid embolism, uterine rupture/laceration, and complications of labor analgesia itself were identified as likely causes in patients who had received labor analgesia, possibly related to a higher frequency of induction of labor in this group.
